entries.task_id: will|have|to wait for *something else* to finish somewhere else
entries.description: will have to wait for *something else* to finish somewhere else
entries.subject: will
entries.object: to wait for *something else* to finish somewhere else

spans.text: Asynchronous code just means that the language 💬 has a way to tell the computer / program 🤖 that at some point in the code, it 🤖 will have to wait for *something else* to finish somewhere else.
And it 🤖 will see if any of the tasks it was waiting for have already finished, doing whatever it had to do.

entries.task_id: program doesn't|have|to be "synchronized" with the slow task
entries.description: program doesn't have to be "synchronized" with the slow task
entries.subject: program doesn't
entries.object: to be "synchronized" with the slow task

spans.text: It's called "asynchronous" because the computer / program doesn't have to be "synchronized" with the slow task, waiting for the exact moment that the task finishes, while doing nothing, to be able to take the task result and continue the work.
